hook.line: A board game found ready to play in a Mesopotamian royal tomb — one of the oldest games whose rules we know.
hook.say: Let me show you the game of kings!

ch.t: From the Royal Tombs of Ur
ch.say: The boards came out of the sand intact.
p: At Tell al-Muqayyar in southern Iraq — ancient Ur — Leonard Woolley excavated the Royal Cemetery in 1922–34 and found five boards.
Boards of the same kind turned up in Iran, Syria, Egypt, Cyprus, Crete and far-off Sri Lanka, and the game reached Kochi in India.

ch.say: Land on a flower and roll again!
ch.cap: The 20-square board with five rosettes. The arrows show the near player’s track
p: Enter on your own four squares, race down the middle row, and finish through your last two. Land on a rival in the middle row to capture it.
The British Museum board (ME 120834) is inlaid with shell, lapis lazuli and red limestone set in bitumen.

ch.say: Rules changed with time and place.
